events.summary: Low coal stocks at thermal plants combined with heat-driven record demand produced rotating power cuts across several states in April-May 2022; Rajasthan, Haryana, Punjab, Uttar Pradesh, Bihar and Madhya Pradesh were reported worst affected, with cuts also reported in Andhra Pradesh, Maharashtra, Gujarat and Jharkhand. The all-India peak shortage reached ~10.77 GW on 28 April 2022 (date = peak day; the episode ran through April-May).
events.effect: All-India peak shortage rose from 5.24 GW (25 Apr) to 10.77-10.78 GW on 28 Apr 2022 with ~192 MU energy not served that day; April energy shortfall ~1.6% of demand (worst month in 6+ years per Reuters analysis); CEA data cited by S&P showed 7,295 MW of coal capacity in outage for fuel shortage on 7 Apr.
events.threshold_basis: Clause 4: generation shortfall forcing rotating load-shedding across multiple states; clause 6 also applies (coal stocks at plants). Cause recorded as 'unknown' because the taxonomy has no fuel-supply-shortfall cause: sources attribute it to low plant coal stocks plus heat-driven demand, and the Coal Secretary disputed that it was a coal crisis.

capacity_affected.source_says: Peak shortage shoots up to 10.77 GW this week (PTI, 1 May 2022); POSOCO put 28 Apr deficit at 10.8 GW

recovery.evidence: National energy deficit reported falling from ~2% in April 2022 to 0.6% in June 2022 (partial normalisation, not zero). Exact end date of load-shedding not established.

events.summary: A 72-hour strike by Chandigarh electricity department staff against privatisation, beginning the night of 21 Feb 2022, was followed by a blackout across large parts of the union territory lasting 36-40 hours. The administration told the High Court the outage resulted from sabotage by striking employees; the army was called in to help restore supply.
events.effect: An official estimated ~40% of Chandigarh without power for 24+ hours; hospitals postponed planned surgeries and water supply was disrupted; outage lasted over 36 hours.
events.threshold_basis: Clause 5: loss of supply to a large population (~40% of a UT of ~1.1 million people, per official estimate) for >36 h. Asset class 'system_wide' (distribution-network outage, no single asset); flagged.

recovery.evidence: Power restored in most parts of the city after 36+ hours; strike withdrawn the evening of 23 Feb 2022 (some sectors still out that afternoon).

events.facility_name: Obra, Anpara and Parichha thermal power stations
events.operator: Uttar Pradesh Rajya Vidyut Utpadan Nigam (state generator); UPPCL distribution
events.summary: A 72-hour strike by Uttar Pradesh power-sector employees from 22:00 on 16 Mar 2023 shut thermal units at Obra, Anpara and Parichha and disrupted distribution; most rural areas were reported without power for two days. The strike was called off on 19 Mar 2023 after talks with the state energy minister.
events.effect: IANS: ~2,392 MW of generation unavailable by the evening of 18 Mar (~17% of 13,856 MW demand) — Obra 1,000 MW, Anpara 1,130 MW, Parichha 210 MW; 506 urban/semi-urban feeders shut affecting ~13 lakh households, rural outages said to be about double. Union claimed 1,850 MW; the power minister said there was no shortage.
events.threshold_basis: Clause 4 (power-plant units >=500 MW aggregate forced offline with reported supply effect) and clause 5 (~1.3 million households on urban feeders alone).

capacity_affected.source_says: 2,392 MW power generation, which is 17 per cent of the total 13,856 MW demand, was not available (IANS). Union figure: 1,850 MW. Plant figures sum to 2,340 MW.

recovery.evidence: Strike called off ~15:00 on 19 Mar 2023 (FPJ). No source reviewed states when the shut units resynchronised or when supply normalised; the end of the cause is not recorded as restoration.

events.operator: Reliance Industries (Sikka); Nayara Energy (Vadinar); Adani Ports (Mundra); Deendayal Port Authority (Kandla)
events.summary: Ahead of Cyclone Biparjoy's landfall in Gujarat (15-16 Jun 2023), Gujarat ports suspended operations: Reliance halted diesel and other product exports from Sikka (serving the Jamnagar refinery), the Gujarat Maritime Board reported oil ports Vadinar and Sikka suspended, and Mundra (incl. a coal import terminal) and Kandla halted vessel operations. Nayara said its refinery was not shut but directed vessels not to enter Vadinar port limits.
events.effect: Product exports from Sikka halted (Reuters); vessel operations suspended at Vadinar, Mundra, Kandla and Tuna. No refinery shutdown reported.
events.threshold_basis: Clause 2: energy import/export terminals suspended operations (precautionary, weather-driven). No refinery throughput effect reported, so clause 1 is NOT claimed.

recovery.evidence: Reliance resumed vessel operations at Sikka on 19 Jun 2023 (Reuters via ThePrint); Kandla and Pipavav reported resumption around 17 Jun. Vadinar/Mundra resumption dates not separately confirmed.

events.facility_name: Nathpa Jhakri (1,500 MW); Parbati-III (520 MW); Larji (126 MW) and others
events.summary: Heavy rain and floods in the second week of July 2023 forced most Himachal hydro stations to shut for silt and flood risk, cutting state generation to about 10% of installed capacity. A parliamentary reply lists Nathpa Jhakri (1,500 MW) shut 9-13 Jul 2023 and Parbati-III (520 MW) shut 8-27 Jul 2023; the 126 MW Larji station was damaged and stayed out of service.
events.effect: State hydro generation fell to ~10% of installed capacity; Nathpa Jhakri lost ~Rs 26.07 crore revenue and Parbati-III ~Rs 35.45 crore (parliamentary reply); HP had to buy power from other states.
events.threshold_basis: Clause 4: units of >=500 MW plants (Nathpa Jhakri, Parbati-III) forced offline with an officially reported outage period. Silt-driven shutdowns are routine at low levels; this one is included because of its scale (state output to ~10%).

capacity_affected.source_says: Nathpa Jhakri 1500 ... 09-07-2023 to 13-07-2023; Parbati-III 520 MW offline 8-27 July 2023 (Lok Sabha/Rajya Sabha reply)

recovery.evidence: State generation back above 90% of capacity by 7 Aug 2023 (HP Power Secretary); Nathpa Jhakri back after 13 Jul and Parbati-III after 27 Jul per the parliamentary table. Larji not restored until May 2025 (physical reconstitution, below threshold).

recovery.evidence: 1,610 of 1,812 feeders restored by 5 Dec 2023 (TANGEDCO CMD); 80% of supply restored per Chief Secretary; lagging localities restored up to 8 Dec.

events.summary: A fire on 20 Apr 2026 in the crude distillation unit section of the 9 Mtpa HPCL Rajasthan refinery, then in commissioning, led HPCL to isolate the CDU, the vacuum distillation unit and all units in the CDU section; the Prime Minister's inauguration the next day was postponed. events.effect: Crude processing at the refinery halted and commissioning/ramp-up disrupted for ~2 months. Kpler: plant not yet contributing to the national product pool, so market supply impact limited; HPCL: impact not expected to be material.

recovery.evidence: HPCL announced in a stock-exchange filing on 18 Jun 2026 that the CDU had restarted after restoration work (date is the announcement date; restart on or before). Refinery had begun producing LPG, petcoke, naphtha and BS-VI diesel.
